items.label: A
items.critique: Flat, friendly, slightly odd shopkeeper small talk ('Your money is still good with me') with a missing comma, exactly Nox's casual register. No backstory, no scene-setting.

items.label: B
items.critique: Exclamation-mark welcomes and a cheesy 'one stop shop for all your literary needs' pun are pure Westwood shop barks.

items.label: C
items.critique: Every keeper opens with suspicion and a mini-story about a third-party faction; dialect ('bold as you like', 'I'll not') and the ellipsis beat are literary, not Nox's sunny shop greeting.

items.label: D
items.critique: 'Aye mate?', 'Ya need some new weapons and armor? This is the place!' and a stiff institutional magic-shop line: the uneven, cheerful voice-acting copy of the campaign.

items.label: E
items.critique: All three keepers riff on the same local monster nuisance with vivid similes ('quick as rats', 'glass and all'); a shared theme across shops and semicolon rhythm give it away.

items.label: F
items.critique: Wistful, quiet prose about stopped mill wheels; clipped declaratives ('Have one.') and a mood piece where Nox would just sell you a sword.

items.label: G
items.critique: Boastful, plot-hooked sales talk ('finest assortment of arms in the South!', 'lad', offering lower prices if you reclaim the [Thing]) is classic campaign shopkeeper.

items.label: H
items.critique: Reeve's levy, pikes paid in promises, 'Don't tell the reeve': civic-economy worldbuilding and wry understatement unlike Nox's broad welcomes.

items.label: I
items.critique: Each keeper gives a melancholy local history (grandfather's lamp, a shut road, a missing carter); fatalistic tone ('Everything's cheap') and semicolons are not Nox.

items.label: J
items.critique: 'At your service! What can I do for you, sir [Class]?' and a rival-inn comparison: plain, upbeat, exclamatory Westwood greetings.

tells: Westwood shopkeepers greet and sell: 'Welcome to X! How can I help you?', exclamation marks, boasts of 'the finest', occasional pun; the new texts open with local grievances or history instead of a welcome.
The new texts tie all three shops in a place to one shared local theme (a closed road, a monster nuisance, stopped mills, a levy); Westwood's three keepers are independent and generic.
Literary devices absent from Nox: semicolon-joined clauses, ellipsis pauses, similes, wry understatement, archaic-British dialect ('I'll not', 'You've none').
Mood: Westwood is chipper and slightly hokey; the new texts are wistful, suspicious or fatalistic.
Westwood addresses the player directly by role ('sir [Class]', 'lad', 'sir') and makes a sales pitch; the new texts rarely name what is sold or pitch it.
